notes: This catalog describes acceptance requirements and is not execution authorization.
An offline consumer may inspect supplied evidence but must not start a Worker, replay a webhook, resume a historical Task, or contact an upstream repository.
Future execution uses an isolated database and mocked outbound transports unless separately authorized for an exact live scope.
Preserve historical sealed reports, receipts, outcomes, identifiers, source pins, and media; record follow-up conclusions separately.
A missing fixture, original query, source revision, or required observation remains not_run. Do not manufacture an input or infer an assertion result from a historical aggregate.

scenarios.title: Resolve the historical Peek loading observation

historicalStatus.scope: The original Peek execution, shared with the navigation/disposal follow-up
historicalStatus.notes: The application remained loading. The aggregate does not identify which individual assertion belongs to this follow-up and does not establish a PR regression.

input.origin: The original Peek sealed report and its retained source/build/execution artifacts
knownFacts: Seven assertions were recorded; PNG and MP4 evidence includes an unsuccessful loading state.
requiredFields: Original Task, Attempt, execution, feature, and assertion identifiers with sealed report digest
Pinned repository, base/head/source revisions, build policy, and sealed build output identity
Exact file fixture bytes or immutable digest plus retrievable artifact, file type, launch arguments, and original loading assertion
Original application configuration, dependency prerequisites, observed result, and timeout
input.notes: The source documents do not provide the original exact file fixture, pinned Peek revision, or per-assertion inputs. Extract them from the sealed evidence before a future run.

preconditions: The complete original input manifest has been recovered and linked without changing its sealed report.
A future authorized Windows execution environment can build and launch the pinned application with the recorded prerequisites.
The acceptance run has a new identity, isolated state, publication disabled, and owned process/window tracking.
positiveControls: Establish that the intended owned Peek window is active and can load a known supported control fixture in the same configured session.
Record the control fixture and expected rendered content from the source and retained evidence; a responsive window or successful build alone is insufficient.
requiredEvidence: Original sealed report reference and digest, recovered input manifest, new run identity, and pinned source/build identity
Owned process/window identity, actual loading transition and rendered result, timestamps, configured timeout, and positive-control observation
Per-assertion result and matching PNG/MP4 observations, including the loading failure if it persists
Confirmed owned-process exit, workspace cleanup, and execution/desktop lease release
passCriteria: Every recovered loading assertion is exercised against its exact fixture and passes with actual rendered content after the positive control passes.
Required evidence is complete, correlated to the new run, and cleanup is confirmed.
The new result is stored independently and the original two/four/one aggregate remains unchanged.
failCriteria: With prerequisites and the positive control satisfied, a recovered loading assertion fails or the application remains loading beyond its recorded timeout.
Owned-process or workspace cleanup fails after an executed run.
A failure describes observed behavior; attributing it to the PR additionally requires a supported comparison that isolates the cause.
notRunCriteria: The exact original fixture, source pin, assertion mapping, or required evidence is unavailable.
The designated Windows execution environment is unavailable, build/prerequisites fail, or the positive control cannot establish a valid loading test.
Only build success, comment/media playback, usage accounting, or recorded-result recovery is available.
cleanup: Stop only the owned application and recording processes and retain their identity receipts.
Confirm owned workspace cleanup and lease release through the managed cleanup protocol.
Keep original sealed reports and media; retain new failure evidence before deleting disposable run data.

scenarios.title: Exercise Peek cross-file navigation and disposal

historicalStatus.scope: The original Peek execution, shared with the loading follow-up
historicalStatus.notes: Attempted navigation did not establish the changed disposal behavior. Cross-file disposal was not exercised; no per-feature count is inferred from the aggregate.

input.origin: The original Peek sealed report, pinned changed-source scope, and retained fixture artifacts
knownFacts: The observed loading state prevented establishing cross-file disposal behavior.
requiredFields: Original sealed report digest and feature/assertion identity mapping
Pinned source/build identity and the exact changed disposal/navigation expectations supported by that source
Original ordered file fixtures with bytes/digests, file types, navigation actions, and expected rendered state at each step
A supported observable disposal condition and its evidence method, including the resource identity and measurement boundary
input.notes: Do not invent file names, formats, navigation keystrokes, resource-release rules, or fixture ordering from the historical aggregate.

preconditions: Recover the exact original navigation/disposal inputs and source-supported observation method.
Resolve the loading prerequisite for the intended files in the future configured Windows environment.
Use a new run identity and isolated state with external publication disabled.
positiveControls: Show the first fixture's actual rendered content before navigation in the same owned application session.
Show the next fixture can render independently so an absent post-navigation preview is not misclassified as disposal success.
requiredEvidence: Original input manifest and immutable report references linked to the new run and build
Owned process/window identity and positive controls for both fixtures
Timestamped navigation observations proving a transition between the actual fixtures
Source-supported disposal observation tied to the exact previous resource, followed by the expected new rendered state
Per-assertion PNG/MP4 evidence and confirmed managed cleanup
passCriteria: All recovered navigation and disposal assertions are executed after their positive controls and pass using the supported observation method.
The evidence establishes both file transition and the changed disposal behavior, with confirmed cleanup.
The original unexercised disposal result and aggregate remain unchanged.
failCriteria: With valid fixtures, prerequisites, and controls, the expected navigation or disposal observation fails.
Owned cleanup fails after execution; record that separately from the feature observation.
notRunCriteria: Any exact fixture, ordering, source pin, assertion mapping, or supported disposal observation is missing.
Loading or independent rendering controls fail, preventing the intended cross-file transition.
Only launch, attempted navigation, window closure, build success, or general memory readings are available.
cleanup: Preserve the before/after resource observations and feature media before managed teardown.
Confirm owned process exit, owned workspace cleanup, and execution/desktop lease release.
Do not use deletion of a shared file or an unrelated process as evidence of disposal.

scenarios.title: Recheck the historical Launcher unit-conversion scenarios

historicalStatus.notes: The sqmi target-operand scenario produced 1 mi² in the actual result control. A selector returned the literal label Title in the failed scenario; two blocked scenarios had no matching result row. None establishes a PR regression by itself.

input.origin: The original Launcher sealed report, four registered feature scenarios, and retained source/build/media artifacts
knownFacts: The historical sqmi target-operand result was 1 mi²; the source documents do not disclose its complete query string.
requiredFields: Original Task/Attempt/execution identifiers, report digest, and all four feature/assertion mappings
Pinned Launcher source revision, sealed build identity, UnitConverter plugin state, locale, and launch mode
Exact query text, encoding, expected result row, and source-supported expected result for every original scenario
Exact historical sqmi control query and actual control/value mapping, distinct from static accessibility labels
input.notes: Do not synthesize a complete conversion query from the token sqmi or the result 1 mi². Retrieve the exact queries and expectations from the original sealed evidence.

preconditions: Recover and preserve the complete four-scenario input manifest and exact pinned source/build identity.
A future Windows environment can launch the recorded supported application mode with UnitConverter enabled and intact text encoding.
Map observed input and result controls in a new owned application session; static Title/Path labels are diagnostic metadata.
positiveControls: Replay the exact recovered sqmi target-operand query in the same configured session and observe 1 mi² in the actual UnitConverter result control.
Confirm UnitConverter participation and the actual result-row value before treating an absent matching row as a feature failure.
requiredEvidence: Original sealed report and exact four-query manifest, linked to an independent new run and pinned source/build
Owned process/window identity, plugin configuration, locale, and input encoding
Observed actual query and result control mapping, the positive-control result 1 mi², and each scenario's actual result-row content or qualified absence
Per-scenario assertion result with PNG/MP4 evidence and confirmed managed cleanup
passCriteria: The recovered sqmi positive control and all four original feature scenarios pass against actual result controls with complete evidence.
No literal accessibility label substitutes for a functional result, and cleanup is confirmed.
The new result is independent; the original one-passed/one-failed/two-blocked outcomes remain intact.
failCriteria: A recovered query produces a source-inconsistent actual result after the configured plugin and positive control are established.
A required actual result row is absent after same-session participation and query prerequisites are proved.
Owned cleanup fails after an executed run. Attribution to the PR needs additional supported causal evidence.
notRunCriteria: An original exact query, expected result, source revision, or original feature mapping is unavailable.
The environment, plugin, build, positive control, or actual result-control mapping cannot be established.
Only the literal Title or Path label is observed, or a missing row is recorded without the required positive control.
Repository test builds fail before execution; source reading and successful feature-media playback do not substitute for executed feature assertions.
cleanup: Stop the owned Launcher/application and recording processes using their retained identities.
Confirm workspace cleanup and execution/desktop lease release.
Retain original and new scenario media independently and preserve exact query encoding.

scenarios.title: Establish the boundary and cause of the historical external HTTP 401

historicalStatus.notes: A real CLI-hook redelivery received external HTTP 401 before the local receiver. The cause is not established, and this does not establish Server duplicate handling or full-path redelivery idempotence.

input.origin: The original failed delivery receipt and retained endpoint/relay/receiver diagnostics
knownFacts: The recorded HTTP status is 401 and no second entry into the local receiver was established by that failure.
requiredFields: Original delivery identity, request timestamp, exact route/transport identity, and response receipt
Retained endpoint, authentication-boundary, relay ingress, and receiver logs for the same request
Raw-envelope digest and relevant non-secret configuration identity; redact credentials and signatures from reviewable exports
A bounded evidence statement describing which component issued the response and whether downstream receipt is positively observed or unproved
input.notes: A later successful HTTPS delivery is separate evidence. It does not retrospectively explain the original CLI-hook 401.

preconditions: Obtain read-only retained diagnostics with enough identity and timing information to correlate the exact failed request.
Keep original failed receipts immutable and redact secrets from exported diagnostic evidence.
Any later synthetic reproduction is isolated with mocked upstream/outbound transport; this catalog authorizes no live redelivery.
positiveControls: Demonstrate that the chosen diagnostic source records an independently known received request in its recorded scope before relying on an absent entry.
Distinguish the external authentication boundary from relay receipt and Server receipt by separately identified logs.
requiredEvidence: Immutable original 401 receipt with correlated delivery identity, timestamp, and route
Boundary-specific logs and their retention/coverage limitations, plus the diagnostic positive control
Evidence-supported cause analysis that names the response-producing boundary or explicitly retains an unknown boundary
A separate follow-up record distinguishing observed facts, causal inference, and any isolated reproduction
passCriteria: The exact failed request is correlated to supported boundary diagnostics and the response-producing cause is established with evidence.
The follow-up closes only the diagnostic question; the original receipt remains failed and no Server idempotence or feature acceptance is inferred.
failCriteria: Available complete evidence contradicts the proposed diagnosis or shows a still-unresolved configured authentication/route defect in an independently authorized reproduction.
notRunCriteria: The original receipt, request identity, retained diagnostics, or positive diagnostic control is missing.
Log absence cannot establish non-receipt because retention or recording coverage is unknown.
Only a later cached duplicate succeeds, or the historical cause remains unestablished.
cleanup: Retain the original failed receipt and redacted diagnostic evidence.
Remove only disposable isolated reproduction resources, if a separately authorized reproduction occurred.
Do not modify hooks, credentials, repository settings, or upstream delivery state through the offline consumer.

scenarios.title: Preserve and independently verify the relay cached-duplicate boundary

historicalStatus.notes: Actual standard HTTPS redelivery returned 202 duplicate from the owned relay's cached receipt for the same delivery GUID and original raw bytes. The four then-existing PR #15 Task, Attempt, and invocation identities and spool history were unchanged.

input.origin: The original cached-redelivery receipts for historical review, or a separately identified isolated synthetic fixture for new acceptance
knownFacts: The accepted historical response came from the relay cache; receiverReentryTested=false.
requiredFields: Exact delivery GUID and raw-envelope digest, matched across first delivery and duplicate
Original cached response and spool-history snapshot for historical review
For a new isolated run: fixture manifest, first receiver acknowledgment, cache receipt, and before/after Task/Attempt/invocation/spool identity snapshots
Receiver ingress observations that distinguish cache handling from a second Server request
input.notes: Synthetic fixtures must be explicitly labeled as new fixtures and must not be presented as reconstructed historical payloads.

preconditions: An independent future run uses an isolated relay and Server state with mocked upstream and publication transports.
The first accepted delivery has a correlated durable receipt before the exact envelope is presented to the relay again.
Receiver ingress and identity snapshots cover both delivery observations.
positiveControls: The first delivery demonstrably reaches the isolated Server receiver and produces the matching durable acceptance acknowledgment.
The cached receipt matches that delivery GUID and exact raw-envelope digest.
requiredEvidence: New fixture/run identity or immutable historical receipt reference, delivery GUID, raw-envelope digest, and matching acknowledgments
Relay cache decision and before/after spool history
Receiver ingress count and before/after Task, Attempt, invocation, and execution identity snapshots
Mock transport record proving zero external repository writes and isolated resource cleanup
passCriteria: The exact duplicate receives the matching cached 202 duplicate response without another Server receiver entry.
Spool history and Task/Attempt/invocation/execution identities remain unchanged after the cached duplicate.
The result explicitly records receiverReentryTested=false and claims only the relay cache boundary.
failCriteria: The cached response mismatches delivery identity or content, or duplicate handling creates additional state/work.
A request enters the Server again when the asserted cache path is expected; record the actual path instead of accepting a cached-boundary claim.
Any external repository write occurs in an isolated run.
notRunCriteria: First-delivery acknowledgment, exact-envelope correlation, receiver ingress coverage, or identity snapshots are unavailable.
The supplied evidence only covers native Server duplicate handling or relay process restart.
Only historical narrative is available without the required receipt artifacts for an independent acceptance result.
cleanup: Retain the correlated cache/receiver receipts and before/after snapshots.
Stop only isolated test processes and remove only owned disposable fixture databases after evidence retention.
Preserve historical spool/Server databases and do not replay historical Tasks.

scenarios.title: Verify a genuine second entry into the native Server receiver

historicalStatus.notes: Earlier native duplicate and committed-Task recovery checks retain their own evidence. The real HTTPS cached duplicate did not enter the Server twice and cannot accept this boundary.

input.origin: A separately identified isolated native-Server fixture and its evidence; exact historical native receipts are required for any historical claim
knownFacts: The relay cache path must not hide the second native Server request.
requiredFields: New isolated fixture/run identity, exact signed synthetic envelope, delivery GUID, and raw-envelope digest
Native Server receiver request/response receipts for two separate entries and a third entry after Server restart using the same GUID and bytes
After-first, after-second, and post-restart persisted delivery, Task, Attempt, model-invocation, and execution identity snapshots
Deterministic fixture processing completion boundary and mocked provider/upstream/outbound logs
input.notes: The initial request may pass through the relay, but subsequent native re-entry requests must bypass only its cache. Retain both Server and relay databases during restart. The offline consumer only reads receipts; it sends no requests.

preconditions: Future execution uses an isolated application database, native Server receiver, deterministic synthetic processing, and mocked external transports.
The first request's committed intake and any fixture-created Task are observable before capturing the comparison baseline.

Evidence can prove two actual native receiver entries plus a third entry after restarting the Server with its unchanged database, and distinguish intake acknowledgment from Task creation or execution.
positiveControls: The first valid signed fixture request reaches the native receiver, returns a matching 202 accepted acknowledgment, and commits the expected intake receipt.
The fixture's initial processing reaches its declared deterministic boundary so later state comparisons cannot hide asynchronous first-request work.
requiredEvidence: Source revision, new fixture/run identity, exact-envelope digest, delivery GUID, and isolated database identity
Three distinct native receiver ingress receipts and matching response bodies and statuses, including the re-entry after restart
Durable canonical delivery identity and after-first/after-second/post-restart Task/Attempt/invocation/execution snapshots at the declared processing boundary
Server restart receipt with the same database identity, preserved canonical record, and no idempotency clearing or historical Task replay
Mocked upstream/provider/outbound call records, zero external repository writes, and owned fixture cleanup
passCriteria: Two native receiver entries are proved for identical delivery identity and raw bytes; the second returns matching 202 duplicate, and a third request returns the same duplicate after Server restart with its retained database.
The same canonical receipt is reused and no additional Task, Attempt, model invocation, or desktop execution is caused by the duplicate.
The result records receiverReentryTested=true and the bounded Server restart observation; it remains separate from relay cached duplicate, physical power-loss, and full live HTTPS claims.
External repository writes are zero and owned fixture cleanup is confirmed.
failCriteria: The exact duplicate creates another canonical intake record, Task, Attempt, invocation, or desktop execution.
The native duplicate acknowledgment mismatches the GUID or returns an unexpected acceptance state.
Any external repository write occurs in the isolated run or an owned fixture cannot be cleaned up.
notRunCriteria: Only a relay cached acknowledgment is present, fewer than two native ingress receipts exist, or the required post-restart re-entry evidence is absent.
Exact raw-envelope identity, deterministic baseline, persisted identity snapshots, or required mock transport records are missing.
An actual authorized execution environment is unavailable; source implementation or test definitions alone cannot pass this scenario.
cleanup: Retain all receiver and restart receipts, the canonical intake record, identity snapshots, and mock call logs.
Stop only owned isolated processes and dispose of only owned fixture databases after evidence retention.
Do not retry or resume any historical Task, modify retained production state, or contact an actual upstream repository.
